title: Computer networks
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Understand how networks and the internet work, layer by layer: delay, loss and throughput, layering, HTTP, DNS and other application protocols, sockets, UDP and TCP, flow and congestion control, IP addressing and subnetting, routing, NAT, the link layer, and network security with TLS.
primary_reading: Computer Networks: A Systems Approach (free textbook)

weeks.1: Network basics: delay, loss and throughput
weeks.8: The network layer: IP addressing and subnetting
weeks.9: Routing algorithms: link state and distance vector
weeks.10: Internet routing: OSPF, BGP and NAT
weeks.11: The link layer: Ethernet, switches and Wi-Fi
weeks.12: Network security: TLS, firewalls and attacks

blocks.deliverable: Trace an HTTP exchange and a DNS lookup.
Trace a TCP connection with its sequence numbers.
Week 7 midterm; subnet an address block.
Run Dijkstra's algorithm and Bellman–Ford on a network.
Explain how TLS protects a connection.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Write a simulator in Python for a reliable transport protocol (stop-and-wait, then a sliding window) over a lossy channel, measure throughput as the loss rate changes, and write a report that links the results to the design of TCP.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
